title: Largest-root bound for mixed characteristic polynomials
statement:
**Theorem.** Let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ be Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^m A_i=I$ and $\operatorname{tr}(A_i)\le\varepsilon$ for all $i$. Define
$$
\mu[A_1,\ldots,A_m](x):=\left.\left(\prod_{i=1}^m(1-\partial_{z_i})\right)\det\left(xI+\sum_{i=1}^m z_iA_i\right)\right|_{z_1=\cdots=z_m=0}.
$$
Then the largest root of $\mu[A_1,\ldots,A_m](x)$ is at most $(1+\sqrt{\varepsilon})^2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13674), page 16. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Constructive selection algorithm for the Akemann–Weaver Lyapunov-type theorem
statement:
Given a finite Bessel sequence $\Phi=\{u_j\}_{j\in J}\subset\mathbb C^n$ with Bessel bound $B=1$, meaning $\sum_{j\in J}u_ju_j^*\le I$, suppose that $\|u_j\|^2\le\varepsilon$ for every $j\in J$, where $\varepsilon>0$. For arbitrary scalars $t_j\in[0,1]$, Theorem 2 asserts that there exists a subset $J'\subset J$ such that
$$
\left\|\sum_{j\in J'}u_ju_j^*-\sum_{j\in J}t_ju_ju_j^*\right\|=O(\varepsilon^{1/8}).
$$
Find a constructive algorithm producing such a subset $J'$ under these hypotheses.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13674), page 32. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Dimension of trivariate $C^1$ splines on generic bipyramid cells
statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a bipyramid cell with $n$ coplanar boundary vertices and let $m$ be the number of distinct slopes determined by the coplanar interior edges $[v_0,v_i]$. In the generic case—$v_{n+1}$ and $v_{n+2}$ are not collinear with $v_0$, and the plane through $v_0,v_{n+1},v_{n+2}$ contains no other $v_i$—the conjecture is that, in every case where Theorem 4 gives only bounds, the dimension of the $C^1$ spline space equals the stated upper bound. Thus, for $d\ge 3$ and $m\ge 3$, conjecturally
$$\dim S^1_d(\Delta)=2n\binom{d}{3}+6d-1+(4-m)^+,$$
and, for $m=2$ and $d\ge 3$, conjecturally
$$\dim S^1_d(\Delta)=8\binom{d}{3}+8d-3-(4-d)^+,$$
where $(x)^+=\max\{x,0\}$. (The report separately states the exact value $\dim S^1_2(\Delta)=11$ when $m=2$.)
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13678), page 46. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Primitive embedding with a prescribed number of roots
statement: For the lattice $L=K_d^{\perp}$, the orthogonal complement of the rank-two saturated lattice $K_d=\langle h^2,T\rangle$ of discriminant $d$ in $(+1)^{\oplus 21}\oplus(-1)^{\oplus 2}\simeq H^4(X,\mathbb Z)$, with its pairing multiplied by $-1$, find a primitive embedding $L\hookrightarrow L_{2,26}:=U^{\oplus 2}\oplus E_8(-1)^{\oplus 3}$ such that $L^{\perp}$ contains at least two and at most twelve vectors of norm $-2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13853), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bhargava’s conjecture on the proportion of soluble ternary cubics
statement:
Let $\rho(P,B)$ denote the proportion of ternary cubics $F(x,y,z)$ with integer coefficients and height $H(F)\le B$, where $H(F)$ is the maximum absolute value of the coefficients, that satisfy a property $P$. If $\mathrm{SOLUBLE}$ denotes having a rational point and $c=0.97256076\ldots$ is the limiting proportion of everywhere locally soluble ternary cubics, then Bhargava conjectures that

$$\lim_{B\to\infty}\rho(\mathrm{SOLUBLE},B)=\frac{1}{3}c.$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13853), page 41. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Universality of eigenvalue gaps for general β-ensembles
statement:
Determine the bulk and edge distributions of the normalized consecutive eigenvalue gaps for the general β-ensemble
\[
dP_N^V(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N)=\frac{1}{Z_N^V}\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|^\beta\exp\!\left(-N\sum_{i=1}^N V(\lambda_i)\right)d\lambda_1\cdots d\lambda_N,
\]
where \(V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is smooth and uniformly convex. The report’s Theorem 2 answers the bulk question: if \(i/N\to\alpha\in(0,1)\), then the local gap statistics under \(P_N^V\), after rescaling by \(T_0'(\gamma_\alpha)\), agree asymptotically with those for the Gaussian ensemble; consequently the bulk gaps have the sine-kernel law. The report also states an analogous comparison at the edge.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13857), page 6. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Evolutionary relaxation for nonlinear rate-independent material models without an internal length scale
statement: For nonlinear material models without an internal length scale, given approximate incremental solutions with time steps and error levels satisfying \$\tau_n,\varepsilon_n\to0$\\, (1) establish convergence of a suitable subsequence of the piecewise-constant interpolants \$q_{\tau_n,\varepsilon_n}$\\, (2) identify a limit \$q:[0,T]\to Q$\\, and (3) determine an evolution equation for every such limit \$q$\\.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13948), page 22. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Füredi–Maleki conjecture on maximizing non-triangular edges
statement: Let $G(a,b,c)$ be the graph consisting of a clique $A$ of size $a$ and two independent sets $B$ and $C$ of sizes $b$ and $c$, respectively, with every vertex of $B$ joined to all vertices of $A\cup C$ and no edges between $A$ and $C$. Let $s(G)$ be the number of non-triangular edges of $G$, and let $s(n,e)$ be the maximum of $s(G)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs with at least $e$ edges. **Conjecture.** For every $n$ and $e$, there is a graph $H=G(a,b,c)$ with $n$ vertices and at least $e$ edges such that $s(H)=s(n,e)$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14604), page 45. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Successive minimum spanning tree costs converge
statement: Let $K_n$ be the complete graph with independent edge costs distributed either uniformly on $[0,1]$ or exponentially with parameter $1$. Let $T_1$ be a minimum-cost spanning tree, and, recursively, let $T_k$ be a minimum-cost spanning tree in the graph obtained from $K_n$ by deleting the edges of $T_1\cup\cdots\cup T_{k-1}$. Then, for each $k\ge 1$, there exists a constant $\gamma_k$ such that, as $n\to\infty$, $c(T_k)\xrightarrow{p}\gamma_k$ for both cost distributions.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14604), page 62. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: General isothermal two-phase Riemann problem for thermodynamically consistent equations of state
statement: For the one-dimensional isothermal Euler system $\partial_t\rho+\partial_x(\rho u)=0$, $\partial_t(\rho u)+\partial_x(\rho u^2+p)=0$, with liquid and vapor phases distinguished by their equations of state, a sharp phase boundary satisfying $[[\rho(u-w)]]=0$, $\rho(u-w)[[u]]+[[p]]=0$, and the kinetic relation $z=\tau p_V[[g+e_{\mathrm{kin}}]]$ where $z=-\rho(u-w)$, determine whether the existence and uniqueness results for the two-phase Riemann problem remain valid when the two specific linear equations of state used in [1] are replaced by arbitrary, thermodynamically consistent equations of state suitable for solving the single-phase Riemann problem.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/30](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14612), page 50. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Euclidean mixed isoperimetric–isodiametric inequality
statement:
For every bounded open set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) with smooth boundary,

$$n\,\operatorname{Vol}(\Omega)\le \operatorname{rad}(\Omega)\,A(\partial\Omega),$$

where \(\operatorname{rad}(\Omega)\) is the radius of the smallest Euclidean ball containing \(\Omega\), and \(A(\partial\Omega)\) is the \((n-1)\)-dimensional area of its boundary. Equality holds if and only if \(\Omega\) is a Euclidean round ball.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/34](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14742), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Determine the decomposition threshold $c_{q,r}$
statement: For integers $q>r\ge 2$, determine the supremum $c_{q,r}$ of all $c\in[0,1]$ with the following property: there exists $n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\ge n_0$, every $K_q^{(r)}$-divisible $r$-graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying $\delta(G)\ge (1-c)n$ has a $K_q^{(r)}$-decomposition. Here $\delta(G)$ is the minimum $(r-1)$-degree; $G$ is $K_q^{(r)}$-divisible when, for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|\le r-1$, $\binom{q-|S|}{r-|S|}$ divides the number of edges of the link graph $G(S)$; and a $K_q^{(r)}$-decomposition is a collection of copies of $K_q^{(r)}$ in $G$ in which every edge of $G$ lies in exactly one copy.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15206), page 40. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Is the morphism Ψ an isomorphism for all tame algebras?
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra and let $C\subseteq\operatorname{rep}(A,d)$ be a $\mathrm{GL}(d)$-invariant, irreducible, closed subvariety with $\theta$-stable decomposition $C=m_1C_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}m_rC_r$, where none of the $C_i$ are orbit closures. The theorem gives a natural morphism
\[
\Psi:\operatorname{Sym}^{m_1}\!\bigl(M(C_1)^{\mathrm{ss}}_\theta\bigr)\times\cdots\times\operatorname{Sym}^{m_r}\!\bigl(M(C_r)^{\mathrm{ss}}_\theta\bigr)\longrightarrow M(C)^{\mathrm{ss}}_\theta.
\]
Determine whether or not $\Psi$ is an isomorphism for all tame algebras.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15217), page 35. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Additive Deligne–Simpson problem for Fuchsian equations
statement:
Given points $a_1,\dots,a_p\in\mathbb{C}$ and conjugacy classes $C_0,C_1,\dots,C_p\subset M(n,\mathbb{C})$, determine whether there exists an irreducible Fuchsian differential equation
\[
\frac{dY}{dx}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\frac{A_i}{x-a_i}Y,\qquad A_i\in M(n,\mathbb{C}),
\]
with $A_0:=-\sum_{i=1}^{p}A_i$ and $A_i\in C_i$ for $i=0,\dots,p$, such that $A_0,\dots,A_p$ have no nontrivial simultaneous invariant subspace of $\mathbb{C}^n$; that is, if $W\subsetneq\mathbb{C}^n$ satisfies $A_iW\subseteq W$ for every $i=0,\dots,p$, then $W=\{0\}$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15217), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Conjecture 1 on the largest zero of a mixed characteristic polynomial
statement:
Let \(P\in D_{m,d}\), where \(D_{m,d}\) is the space of homogeneous, doubly stochastic, stable polynomials in \(\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_m]\) of degree \(d\). Here, doubly stochastic means \(\frac{\partial P}{\partial x_i}(\mathbf{1})=\frac{d}{m}\) for every \(1\le i\le m\), with \(\mathbf{1}=(1,\ldots,1)\), and stable means \(P(x)\ne 0\) for every \(x\in\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Im}(z)>0\}^m\). Define
\[
\chi_P(t)=\left.\left(1-\frac{\partial}{\partial x_1}\right)\cdots\left(1-\frac{\partial}{\partial x_m}\right)P\right|_{x_1=\cdots=x_m=t},
\]
and let \(\lambda_1(P)\) be the largest zero of \(\chi_P\). Is it true that
\[
\lambda_1(P)\le \lambda_1(P_\infty),\qquad P_\infty:=\left(\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_m}{m}\right)^d?
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/14](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15219), page 55. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Highly localized summability kernels on the sphere induced by Newtonian kernels: Problem 1
statement:
For arbitrary constants $M>0$ (large) and $\\varepsilon>0$ (small), construct a function $\\Phi_\\varepsilon(\\eta,x)$ on $S^{d-1}\\times B^d$ of the form
\[
\\Phi_\\varepsilon(\\eta,x)=\\sum_{j=1}^{K}\\frac{b_j}{|x-y_j|^{d-2}}\quad(d>2),
\]
or
\[
\\Phi_\\varepsilon(\\eta,x)=\\sum_{j=1}^{K}b_j\\ln|x-y_j|\quad(d=2),
\]
with $|y_j|>1$, $b_j\\in\\mathbb R$ depending on $\\eta$, $M$, and $d$, and $K$ depending only on $M$ and $d$, such that
\[
|\\Phi_\\varepsilon(\\eta,x)|\\le c\\varepsilon^{-d+1}
\\bigl(1+\\varepsilon^{-1}|x-\\eta|\\bigr)^{-M},
\\qquad\\forall x,\\eta\\in S^{d-1},
\]
and
\[
\\int_{S^{d-1}}\\Phi_\\varepsilon(\\eta,x)\\,d\\sigma(x)=1,
\\qquad\\forall\\eta\\in S^{d-1},
\]
where $c>0$ depends only on $M$ and $d$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15222), page 31. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Flag-algebra upper bound for a specified forbidden-family Turán density
statement:
Let \(\mathcal L\) be the family of the following nine 3-uniform hypergraphs:
\[
\begin{aligned}
K^-_4&=\{123,124,134\},\\
C^-_5&=\{123,124,135,245\},\\
C^+_5&=\{123,124,135,146,156\},\\
L_2&=\{123,124,125,136,456\},\\
L_3&=\{123,124,135,256,346\},\\
L_4&=\{123,124,156,256,345\},\\
L_5&=\{123,124,145,346,356\},\\
L_6&=\{123,124,145,346,356\},\\
P^-_7&=\{123,145,167,246,257,347\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal L)\) is the maximum number of edges in a 3-uniform hypergraph on \(n\) vertices containing no member of \(\mathcal L\) as a subhypergraph. The report states the claim
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal L)}{\binom n3}<0.25072.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/19](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15427), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Unique maximum-likelihood estimator for multivariate Gaussian MTP₂ models
statement:
The report states that, for a multivariate Gaussian distribution in the MTP₂ model, the maximum-likelihood problem is a convex optimization problem with a unique solution whenever the number of observations is at least two. Writing the solution as $\hat K=\hat\Sigma^{-1}$ and the sample covariance matrix as $S=\{s_{uv}\}$, it is characterized by

$$
\hat k_{uv}\le 0\quad\text{for all }u\ne v,
$$
$$
\hat\sigma_{vv}-s_{vv}=0\quad\text{for all }v\in V,
$$
$$
\hat\sigma_{uv}-s_{uv}\ge 0\quad\text{for all }u\ne v,
$$
$$
(\hat\sigma_{uv}-s_{uv})\hat k_{uv}=0\quad\text{for all }u\ne v.
$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15428), page 15. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Sharp posterior phase transition for overfitted hidden Markov models
statement:
For an overfitted hidden Markov model with true state number $K^*<K$, determine—possibly using techniques from algebraic statistics—the posterior behavior of the extra states, in particular whether one can obtain a sharp phase-transition characterization of when they are emptied versus merged with true states. More specifically, under the row-wise Dirichlet prior described on page 57, determine conditions under which
\[
\Pi\!\left(\sum_{j>K^*}\mu_Q(j)>u_n\mid y_{1:n}\right)=o_{P_{\theta^*}}(1)
\]
for some sequence $u_n=o(1)$, and identify sharp thresholds for the Dirichlet hyperparameters separating emptying from merging.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15428), page 57. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Extension of the quaternion-algebra assignment to the canonical component
statement: For a hyperbolic knot $K$, with canonical component $C(K)$ of the $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety and smooth projective model $\widetilde C$, determine whether the assignment $\chi_\alpha\mapsto A_\alpha$ associated with hyperbolic Dehn surgeries extends to an Azumaya algebra over all of $\widetilde C$. The report answers this in Theorem 1: extension holds if the Alexander polynomial satisfies condition $(\star)$, namely, for every root $z$ of $\Delta_K(t)$ and every square root $w$ of $z$, $\mathbb Q(w)=\mathbb Q(w+w^{-1})$; conversely, assuming the point of $\widetilde C$ determined by a nonabelian reducible representation is smooth, failure of $(\star)$ prevents extension.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/38](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15581), page 51. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bourgain’s discretized sum-product theorem
statement:
Let $\alpha>0$ and $\kappa>0$ be positive absolute constants. There exist $\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1>0$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, if $A\subset\delta\mathbb Z$ is finite and satisfies $|A|\ge \delta^\alpha$ and
\[
|A\cap I|\le \ell(I)^\kappa |A|
\]
for every interval $I$ with $\delta<\ell(I)<\delta^{\varepsilon_0}$, then
\[
\max\{N(A+A,\delta),N(AA,\delta)\}\ge \delta^{-\varepsilon_1}N(A,\delta).
\]
Here $\ell(I)$ is the Lebesgue measure of $I$, and $N(S,\delta)$ is the minimum number of intervals in $\delta\mathbb Z$ intersecting $S$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/47](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15952), page 46. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Maximal $A_k$-singularity on a plane curve of fixed degree
statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb{A}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be an algebraic curve, not necessarily reduced, of degree $d$. An $A_k$-singularity means that, near the singular point, the curve is analytically locally isomorphic to $y^2-x^{k+1}=0$. For $d\ge 1$, what is the maximal $k$ such that there exists such a curve of degree $d$ having an $A_k$-singularity? Denote this maximum by $N(d)$. The report gives $N(1)=0$, $N(2)=1$, $N(3)=3$, $N(4)=7$, $N(5)=12$, and $N(6)=19$, while $N(7)$ is left unknown.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16169), page 52. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Geometry controlling the d-primary Brauer–Manin obstruction
statement:
Determine how the geometry of a smooth projective variety controls the sets of positive integers $d$ for which $BM_d$, $BM_d^{\perp}$, or $\widehat{BM}_d$ holds; equivalently, determine the sets
\[
\{d: BM_d\text{ holds}\},\qquad \{d: BM_d^{\perp}\text{ holds}\},\qquad \{d: \widehat{BM}_d\text{ holds}\}.
\]
Here $BM_d$ means $X(\mathbb A)^{\mathrm{Br}}=\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow X(\mathbb A)^{\mathrm{Br}[d^\infty]}=\varnothing$, $BM_d^{\perp}$ means $X(\mathbb A)\neq\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow X(\mathbb A)^{\mathrm{Br}[d^\perp]}\neq\varnothing$, and $\widehat{BM}_d$ means that for every subgroup $B\subseteq\mathrm{Br}X$, $X(\mathbb A)^B=\varnothing\Longleftrightarrow X(\mathbb A)^{B[d^\infty]}=\varnothing$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16408), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Penrose-type mass–angular momentum inequality for one-ended initial data
statement:
Can one prove, for a three-dimensional, axially symmetric initial data set $(M^3,g,k)$ for the Einstein equations satisfying the dominant energy condition, with one asymptotically flat end and an apparent-horizon boundary, the weaker Penrose-type inequality

$$m^2 \geq \frac{A_{\min}}{16\pi}+\frac{4\pi J^2}{A_{\min}},$$

where $m$ is the mass, $J$ is the angular momentum, and $A_{\min}$ is the minimum area required to enclose one end?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16411), page 64. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Control-functional formulation of Coulomb friction in a fractured poromechanical model
statement:
Determine a suitable functional $J$ and solve the associated control problem: find a slip control $\beta$ such that
\[
\beta=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in B}J\bigl(Cu(\gamma),\gamma\bigr),
\qquad Au(\gamma)=F+H\gamma,
\]
where $B\subset H^{1/2}_{00}(\Gamma)$, $u(\gamma)\in V_h\subset H^1(\Omega_\gamma)$ is determined by
\[
a\bigl(u(\gamma),v\bigr)=F(v)+h(\gamma,v)\qquad\forall v\in V_h,
\]
with
\[
h(\gamma,v)=\int_\Gamma \alpha_t\gamma\cdot\llbracket v_t^\Gamma\rrbracket-\int_\Gamma\{\tau(v)\}\cdot\gamma,
\qquad C u=\{\tau(u)\}.
\]
The functional should be chosen so that minimization approximates the Coulomb-friction conditions.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/39](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16414), page 83. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Geometry of the irreducible components of the maximal flat degeneration
statement: Let $V$) be a complex vector space of dimension $n+1$, and let $\mathrm{Fl}_{\mathrm{mf}}(V)$ be the maximal flat linear degeneration of the complete flag variety, with irreducible components $C(A)$ parametrized by non-crossing arc diagrams $A$. For a non-crossing arc diagram $A$, define $r(A)_{ij}=i-$ the number of arcs in $A$ starting in $\{1,\ldots,i\}$ and ending in $\{i+1,\ldots,j\}$, and let $C(A)$ be the closure of the locus in $\mathrm{Fl}_{\mathrm{mf}}(V)$ satisfying $\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{pr}_{[i,j]}:U_i\to U_j)=r(A)_{ij}$ for all $i<j$. Determine whether the components $C(A)$ are normal, describe their singular loci, determine whether they admit natural closed embeddings into Schubert varieties, and characterize when two such components are isomorphic.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17289), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Quantum operations with a prescribed hypergroup relation
statement:
**Problem 9.** For $A$ a conformal net associated with a lattice [DX06] or a strongly local vertex operator algebra [CKLW18], find $\\phi\in\operatorname{QuOp}(A)$ with
$$
\phi\circ\phi=w^{-1}\operatorname{id}+(1-w^{-1})\phi
$$
for small positive real numbers $w>1$. For example, for the even $A_2\times E_6$ lattice, the hypothetical (see [EG11]) conformal net associated with the Haagerup subfactor would give such an element $\phi$ with $w=\frac{11+3\sqrt{13}}{2}$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17292), page 28. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Detection of non-isotopic surface embeddings by $Z_C$
statement: Determine whether the extended TQFT $Z_C$ can detect non-isotopic embeddings of surfaces into closed three-manifolds. The report answers this negatively for embedded spheres: a sphere labelled by $A$ multiplies $Z_C$ by the embedding-independent factor $\dim(A)$. It answers positively for 2-tori, exhibiting three embeddings into a 3-torus for the modular fusion category of integrable representations of $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_{16}$; the three simple-algebra Morita-class representatives are $A_{17}$, $D_{10}$, and $E_7$, and the corresponding displayed values are respectively $(17,17,17)$, $(34,18,10)$, and $(34,18,7)$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17292), page 65. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Talagrand’s expectation-threshold conjecture
statement: There is a universal constant $K$ such that, for every finite set $X$ and every increasing family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^X$, $q(\mathcal F)\ge q_f(\mathcal F)/K$. Equivalently, if $\mathcal F$ is weakly $p$-small, then it is $(p/K)$-small. Here $q(\mathcal F)$ is the maximum $p$ for which there exists $\mathcal G\subseteq 2^X$ with $\mathcal F\subseteq\langle\mathcal G\rangle$ and $\sum_{S\in\mathcal G}p^{|S|}\le 1/2$, while $q_f(\mathcal F)$ is the maximum $p$ for which there exists $g:2^X\to\mathbb R_+$ such that $\sum_{S\subseteq T}g(S)\ge1$ for every $T\in\mathcal F$ and $\sum_{S\subseteq X}g(S)p^{|S|}\le1/2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2020/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17464), page 55. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Inf-sup stability of the spectral non-conforming Petrov–Galerkin multiple-traces discretization
statement: For the operator $F(s)$ and spaces defined in Problem 1, let $X_L^\ell:=\operatorname{span}\{\lambda_n^\ell\}_{n=0}^L\subseteq V_{\mathrm{pw},\ell}$ and $Y_L^\ell:=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_n^\ell\}_{n=0}^L\subseteq \widetilde{\widetilde V}_\ell$, and set $X_L:=X_L^0\times\cdots\times X_L^M$ and $Y_L:=Y_L^0\times\cdots\times Y_L^M$. Establish an inf-sup condition for the discrete problem, namely determine whether, for $g=(g_0,g_1,\ldots,g_M)\in V_M$, there exists a unique $\lambda\in X_L$ satisfying $(F(s)\lambda,\phi)_\times=(g,\phi)_\times$ for every $\phi\in Y_L$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2020/5](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17468), page 63. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Sharp bounds for approximation in $C_k([0,1]^d)$ when $k\ge 3$ is odd
statement:
For odd integers $k\ge 3$, determine the sharp dependence on $d$ and $n$ of the $n$th minimal worst-case $L_\infty$-approximation error $e_n(C_k([0,1]^d),\mathrm{APP})$, closing the gap between the reported bounds
\[
\min\!\bigl(\varepsilon_k,c_k d^{k/2}n^{-k/d}\bigr)
\le e_n(C_k([0,1]^d),\mathrm{APP})
\le \min\!\bigl(1,\widetilde c_k d^{(k+1)/2}n^{-k/d}\bigr),
\]
which hold for all $n,d\in\mathbb N$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2020/6](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17469), page 12. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Sós–Verstraëte conjecture on hypergraphs with no tight cycles
statement: For an integer $r\ge 3$, let $f_r(n)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no tight cycle, where a tight cycle is a sequence of at least $r+1$ distinct vertices such that every $r$ consecutive vertices, with indices taken modulo the cycle length, form an edge. Sós and, independently, Verstraëte conjectured that, for all sufficiently large $n$, $$f_r(n)=\binom{n-1}{r-1}.$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/10252930), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Standard clique edge-weighting conjecture and stability
statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph. For an edge $e\in E(G)$, let $r$ be the order of the largest clique in $G$ containing $e$, and assign it weight $w(e)=\frac{r}{2(r-1)}$. Write $w(G)=\sum_{e\in E(G)}w(e)$. For every $n$-vertex graph $G$,
\[
w(G)\leq \left(\frac14+o(1)\right)n^2.
\]
Moreover, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $n_0$ such that if $w(G)=\left(\frac14+o(1)\right)n^2$ and $n\geq n_0$, then $G$ is within edit distance at most $\varepsilon n^2$ of some Turán graph.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/10252930), page 64. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: General Fourier restriction estimates for smooth hypersurfaces
statement:
For a sufficiently smooth hypersurface $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, determine the range of exponents $(\widetilde p,\widetilde q)$ for which the a priori estimate
\[
\left(\int_S |\widehat f|^{\widetilde q}\,d\sigma\right)^{1/\widetilde q}\le C\|f\|_{L^{\widetilde p}(\mathbb{R}^n)}
\]
holds for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^n)$, where $d\sigma$ is Riemannian surface measure on $S$. The report states that this general $L^{\widetilde p}$–$L^{\widetilde q}$ question remains wide open.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/31](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11101912), page 9. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Local CLT and lower bound for the annealed second heat-kernel derivative
statement: Under Assumptions 1 and 2, determine whether one can establish a local central limit theorem and a corresponding lower bound for the annealed second spatial derivative of the heat kernel, in particular for the mixed derivative \(\nabla_x^2\nabla_{x'}^2\bar p_{0,t}(y,y')\). Here Assumption 1 requires that \(\mathbb P\) is stationary and ergodic under time-space shifts, the conductances are \(\mathbb P\)-a.s. symmetric, and \(\mathbb E[\omega_t(e)]<\infty\) for every edge \(e\in E^d\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\); Assumption 2 requires a deterministic \(C_2>0\) such that \(\mathbb P[\omega_t(x,y)\ge C_2]=1\) for every \((x,y)\in E^d\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11695859), page 72. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Universal families of curves realizing all pants decompositions
statement: Given an orientable surface $S$ of genus $g$, a family of closed curves $\Gamma$ realizes all types of pants decompositions if, for every pants decomposition $P$ of $S$, there is a homeomorphism sending the curves of $P$ to a subset of the curves in $\Gamma$. What is the minimum possible size of such a family $\Gamma$? The report states that only a superlinear lower bound and a singly exponential upper bound are known, leaving open the problem of bridging this gap.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2023/3](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12697686), page 43. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Maximum balanced independent sets in the Boolean cube
statement: For the Boolean cube $Q_r$ with vertex set $\\{0,1\\}^r$ and edges joining pairs at Hamming distance $1$, let $\operatorname{Ev}(r)=\{x\in\{0,1\}^r:|x|\text{ is even}\}$ and $\operatorname{Odd}(r)=\{x\in\{0,1\}^r:|x|\text{ is odd}\}$. Let $\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}(Q_r)$ be the maximum cardinality of an independent set $S\subseteq V(Q_r)$ satisfying $|S\cap\operatorname{Ev}(r)|=|S\cap\operatorname{Odd}(r)|$. Define $a(1)=0$ and, for every integer $k\ge 1$, $a(2k)=2^{2k}-\binom{2k}{k}$ and $a(2k+1)=2a(2k)$. Is it true that, for every integer $r\ge 1$, $\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}(Q_r)=a(r-1)$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2024/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14298804), page 44. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: σ_k-Yamabe problem in the larger cone
statement: Let $(M,g_0)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold and let $[g_0]$ be its conformal class. For $k\ge 2$, define $\mathcal C_{k-1}([g_0])=\Gamma_{k-1}^+\cap[g_0]$, where $\Gamma_{k-1}^+=\{\Lambda\in\mathbb R^n:\sigma_j(\Lambda)>0\text{ for all }j\le k-1\}$. If $\mathcal C_{k-1}([g_0])\ne\varnothing$, find a conformal metric satisfying $\sigma_k(g)=c$ for some constant $c$. The report states that this problem has an affirmative answer.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/11](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299092), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Optimal scheduling of dynamic transport
statement: Given a prescribed transport map $T$ and the interpolation $T_t(x)=tT(x)+(1-t)x$ for $t\in[0,1]$, consider the scheduled family $T_{\tau(t)}(x)$, where $\tau:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ satisfies $\tau'(t)>0$, $\tau(0)=0$, and $\tau(1)=1$. Among such schedules, determine the schedule $\tau$ that minimizes, uniformly over $t\in[0,1]$, the spatial Lipschitz constant of a velocity field $v(\cdot,t)$ whose time-$t$ flow map is $T_{\tau(t)}$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299282), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Computing all-genus Gromov–Witten invariants of \(\operatorname{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{C}^2)\)
statement:
For partitions \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r\) of \(d\), compute, for all genera \(g\), the equivariant Gromov–Witten series
\[
\left\langle \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r\right\rangle^{\operatorname{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{C}^2)}_g
=
\sum_{n\ge 0}q^n\int_{[\mathcal{M}_{g,r}(\operatorname{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{C}^2),\beta_n)]^{\mathrm{vir}}}
\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname{ev}_i^*(|\mu_i\rangle),
\]
where \(\beta_n\) is characterized by \(\int_{\beta_n}D=n\), \(|\mu_i\rangle\) are the \(T\)-equivariant cohomology classes associated to the partitions, and the resulting series lies in \(\mathbb{Q}(t_1,t_2,q)\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299284), page 43. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Maximum diameter of simplicial complexes (Santos upper-bound conjecture)
statement:
For every integer $d\ge 2$, there exists an integer $n_0>0$ such that, for every $n>n_0$, the maximum diameter $H_s(n,d)$ of a strongly connected simplicial $d$-complex on vertex set $[n]$ satisfies
\[
H_s(n,d)=\left\lfloor \frac{1}{d}\binom{n}{d}-\frac{d+1}{d}\right\rfloor.
\]
Here a simplicial $d$-complex is a family of subsets of $[n]$ closed under taking subsets, with every facet of size $d+1$; its dual graph has the facets as vertices, with two facets adjacent when their intersection has size $d$; and $H_s(n,d)$ is the maximum diameter of the dual graph over strongly connected such complexes.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299518), page 68. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Finite length of permutation modules for homogeneous structures
statement: Suppose that $M$ is a structure which is homogeneous in a finite relational language and $G=\operatorname{Aut}(M)$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and consider $G$ acting on $W=M^k$. Is $F^W$ of finite length for every field $F$? Here, a module $U$ has finite length if there is a bound on the length $n$ of a chain of submodules $\{0\}<U_1<U_2<\cdots<U_n=U$; the maximum such length is called the length of $U$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/58](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299587), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: A class of periodic graphs satisfying Ehrhart reciprocity
statement:
Find a reasonable class $P'$ of pairs $(\Gamma,x_0)$, consisting of a periodic graph $\Gamma$ and one of its vertices $x_0$, such that:

- $P'$ contains the class $\{(\Gamma_Q,0)\mid Q\text{ is a reflexive polytope}\}$; and
- for every $(\Gamma,x_0)\in P'$, the corresponding growth sequence satisfies
  $$f_b(-i)=(-1)^n f_b(i-1),\qquad f_s(-i)=(-1)^{n+1}f_s(i),$$
  where $f_b$ and $f_s$ are the quasi-polynomials corresponding to the cumulative and spherical growth sequences, respectively.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/9](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299088), page 29. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Sharp rainbow-triangle constant without an affine plane
statement: For a fixed integer $r$ such that no affine plane of order $r-1$ exists, determine exactly the sharp constant governing the maximum number of rainbow triangles in a simple $r$-edge-colored graph with $m$ edges. The report states that the general upper bound is $\sqrt{\frac{2(r-2)}{9r}}\,m^{3/2}$, while in the absence of an affine plane of order $r-1$ it can be improved to $\left(\sqrt{\frac{2(r-2)}{9r}}-\varepsilon\right)m^{3/2}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending only on $r$. The report gives $r=7$ and $r=11$ as examples.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 41. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Local removal lemma characterization for arbitrary graphs
statement:
**Conjecture.** Let $H$ be a fixed graph on $k$ vertices. A graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is $o(1)$-close to being $H$-free under the $L^\infty$ distance if and only if, for every set of $a(H)$ vertices of $G$, the number of copies of $H$ in which these $a(H)$ vertices form an independent set of the copy is $o(n^{k-a(H)})$.

Here $a(H)$ is the maximum size of an independent subset $A$ of $H$ such that, for every homomorphism $\rho$ from $H$ to itself, if every vertex in $A$ has at most one pre-image under $\rho$, then $\rho$ has exactly $\lvert A\rvert$ vertices mapping to elements of $A$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 57. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Forest Monk’s formula
statement:
Let an indexed forest $F$ be a sequence of plane binary trees $(T_1,T_2,\ldots)$, where $T_i$ is a single leaf for $i$ sufficiently large, and canonically label the union of their leaves by $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ from left to right, tree by tree. Define the forest polynomial $P_F$ by
\[
P_F=\sum_{\kappa}\prod_{v\in F}x_{\kappa(v)},
\]
where $\kappa$ ranges over maps from the internal nodes of $F$ to $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ satisfying, for every internal node $v$ with left and right children $v_L,v_R$, $\kappa(v_L)\geq \kappa(v)$ and $\kappa(v_R)>\kappa(v)$, with the values at leaf children understood as their canonical leaf labels. Determine an explicit expression for the coefficients $a^G_{i,F}$ in the expansion
\[
(x_1+\cdots+x_i)P_F=\sum_G a^G_{i,F}P_G.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/2](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299904), page 67. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

statement:
Prove in the standard unrelativized model that bounded-error quantum polynomial time BQP is not contained in the polynomial hierarchy PH.

Source: [Scott Aaronson, BQP and the Polynomial Hierarchy, arXiv:0910.4698, Abstract (2009).](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.4698).

statement:
Determine whether every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine using O(log n) work space is decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using O(log n) work space; equivalently, decide whether directed s-t reachability belongs to L.
